pr_title: Fix #97736 in MemoryCache.cs with a lock around the TriggerOvercapacityC... method
pr_body:
This solves https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/97736
This PR addresses the excessive CPU and memory usage during the MemoryCache compaction process by limiting the number of concurrent compaction tasks to one. The change ensures that only one thread performs the compaction at any given time, reducing resource spikes and improving overall performance.

review_comments: Does the flag need to be volatile? I'm not sure with the memory model.

Seems to me that it doesn't, since we access it through `Interlocked`.  And when we write to it, there is no need in it being volatile since according to [this](https://igoro.com/archive/volatile-keyword-in-c-memory-model-explained/) write operations are "kind of volatile" and we will see that change anyway.

And we can also follow the examaple from here: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.threading.interlocked.exchange?view=net-8.0

And replace `lockFlag = 0;` with Interlocked.Exchange if needed.

Also the last example provided here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/design/specs/Memory-model.md Shown that all that we need is a volatile read (in our case `Interlocked.CompareExchange`) and you can have non volatile write and you will still see the changes eventually. So for sure there is no need to change anything.
